problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a function such that ${\int }_{4}^{1}\frac{1}{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=2$ and ${\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=6.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{-1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$

activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Definite Integrals Involving the Limits of Integration

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a function such that ${\int }_{5}^{3}4f(x)\,\text{d}x=-1$ and ${\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=2.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5}^{3}4f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ 4{\int }_{5}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ -4{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ {\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
